The reviewed tree is saved on a private backup branch. I’m resolving the first layer’s conflicts so it contains only chunk meshing and its checks; upload changes belong in the later generation layer.

The chunk layer passes the Bend proof checks. Its native fixtures are running now, including exact canonical order, dirty-neighbor reuse and the independent Body corruption control. The complete interactive acceptance run remains preserved separately.

The chunk layer passes all 15 fixtures, produces identical output with one and six threads, and rejects the corruption control. It is committed. I’m checking the measurement layer next, then the combined upload and generation layer.

The measurement layer passes all 22 protocol checks and is committed. I’m now assembling uploads, native ownership and generation publication into one layer. Keeping them together avoids exposing the earlier partial-retirement defect.

The combined layer passes generator and shader freshness checks. I’m verifying this new intermediate composition before committing it, with sanitizer and Vulkan validation checks for publication rollback, resource retirement and native ownership.

The sanitized generation checks pass, including literal device bytes, reuse, empty-after-edit, reset and cleanup. The retirement checks are now testing rejected publication and preservation of old allocations.

The retirement test has finished compilation and is running on the device. It checks failed publication, mixed generation reuse and the legacy uploader. I’ll verify the whole layer before committing it.

Atomic retirement passes. Rejected publication preserves old bytes, handles, counters and resource rows, and retries succeed for both chunk generations and legacy full or empty replacements. Installation failure recovery is next.

Installation recovery and all six upload fault cases pass under sanitizers. Handled failures preserve installed geometry; reset failure and device loss clean up the installation scope. The native Vulkan probes are now compiling.

The sanitizer build for the native probes is still running. After those probes, the remaining layer checks are presentation ownership, the legacy offscreen consumer and production appearance, including the shadow-causality controls.

The native probes pass, including atomic retirement, failed-reset retention, timestamp ownership and two pending submissions with independent readback. Presentation checks are running now. The staged source tree is unchanged from the start of these checks.

Presentation ownership checks pass, including same-index reacquisition while an older presentation remains unobserved. The legacy offscreen consumer passes its geometry, material, depth, reuse and cleanup checks. Its validation-enabled repeat is running.

The legacy consumer also passes with Khronos and synchronization validation enabled. Production appearance is the final gate for this layer. It checks the original Body reference, rendered coverage and shadow causality.

Production appearance checks are still running. I also traced the intermediate window caller after the retirement changes. It collects old allocations at the next upload; I’m adding native window checks to verify that this PR endpoint stays functional and keeps resource use bounded.

The production renderer and its independent oracle pass in normal mode. The validation-enabled repeat and shadow controls are still running. The subsequent window checks will cover edits, reset, resize, suspension and shutdown on the intermediate layer.

The validation-enabled production renderer passes too. Its independent oracle is still running. Once it finishes, the gate will run five deliberate shadow corruptions, which must each be rejected.

Both production oracles and the actual GPU-depth lighting oracle pass. The shadow-causality gate is now running. No source changes have been needed during the layer checks.

Production appearance passes, and all five shadow corruptions are rejected as expected. The added window checks are now building the intermediate executable. They will verify that this stack layer can run the existing window consumer before frame-slot integration lands.

The intermediate window build is still compiling. I’ve preserved the fresh production reports separately, with sanitizers marked “not requested” for that repeat, so they cannot be confused with the earlier full sanitizer acceptance run.

The intermediate window checks pass with shared queues, split queues and close while suspended. The default Atelier driver is now checking edits, exact reset images, flight, resize and shutdown.

The default Atelier checks pass with both queue configurations. They cover edits, reset images, movement, resize, suspension, remap and zero-row shutdown. The generation layer is verified. I’m committing it, then restoring the saved final tree for the frame layer.

The staged frame tree exactly matches the saved tree that passed full acceptance. The reconstruction rows remain in the working journal. A fresh Bend proof check is running before I commit that exact tree.

All four code layers are committed. The frame commit exactly matches the saved full tree, and all 1,810 accepted producer source hashes match the restored files. I’m recording the delivery mapping and finalizing the PR descriptions before publication.

The delivery mapping is committed, and the working tree is clean. Remote `main` is unchanged and none of the new branches exists there yet. I’m publishing the four branches, then opening and linking each ready PR to its parent.

The four ready PRs are open and linked as one stack: [#10](https://github.com/aivv73/bend-vulkan/pull/10), [#11](https://github.com/aivv73/bend-vulkan/pull/11), [#12](https://github.com/aivv73/bend-vulkan/pull/12) and [#13](https://github.com/aivv73/bend-vulkan/pull/13). GitHub confirms their intended base branches. I’m recording publication receipts before the final independent delivery audit.

The published descriptions keep the performance claim narrow. Exact-image mismatches exclude every old/new timing pair, so no implementation speedup is claimed. The slot numbers describe traced configurations; the final source still matches the fully tested implementation.

The final independent delivery audit is running. Its brief had a count typo: the generation layer ran six sanitizer command groups, including presentation. The archived commands and results list all six correctly.

The final Bend proof check passes. Remote branch heads match the published commits, and T3 still reports all four ready PRs in order. The independent delivery audit is the only remaining gate.

I’m waiting for the independent verdict before recording the final review result. The audit covers the delivery mapping, preserved evidence, branch ancestry and published PRs.

The review is still running. I’m keeping the audit files fixed until it returns so its verdict applies to a stable record.
